text_a: This section is intended for full service clients that issue Visa cards. These issuers have special processing considerations, which this section describes. Visa POS Issuers Visa POS acquirers can choose to send transactions using the full service or the authorization- only processing method. The authorization-only acquirer sends above-floor-limit POS transactions made with a Visa POS card as authorization requests (0100s). One to several days later, the acquirer submits BASE II clearing records (TC 05s and TC 06s). V.I.P. clears these BASE II records to full service issuers as deferred clearing advices (0220s), messages similar to the online deferred clearing advices. As a result, Visa POS issuers that choose to process transactions using the full service method must be prepared to receive online financial transactions from full service acquirers, and to receive authorization messages followed by deferred clearing transactions from full service and authorization-only acquirers. For authorization-only acquired POS transactions, the full service issuer must be prepared to accept authorization requests (0100s) that have no financial impact. The full service issuer may choose to manage the cardholder's available balance or credit line by placing a temporary hold on funds until it receives the 0220 advice. Because there could be circumstances in which the issuer does not receive the 0220 advice (for instance, a reversal was not properly processed), the full service issuer may want to establish an expiration date for holds, possibly three to four days after the authorization date. Another consideration for full service issuers is that for cross-currency transactions from authorization-only acquirers, the cardholder billing amount in the 0220 message may be different from the amount authorized. This difference may be due to fluctuations in currency conversion rates between the date of the authorization and the date that the transaction clears. Full service issuers also need to remember that acquirers may not know the final amount at the time of authorization and that some transactions may not have required an authorization because they were below the floor limit.

Visa POS Issuers Visa POS acquirers can choose to send transactions using the full service or the authorization- only processing method. The authorization-only acquirer sends above-floor-limit POS transactions made with a Visa POS card as authorization requests (0100s). One to several days

later, the acquirer submits BASE II clearing records (TC 05s and TC 06s). V.I.P. clears these BASE II records to full service issuers as deferred clearing advices (0220s), messages similar to the online deferred clearing advices. As a result, Visa POS issuers that choose to process transactions using the full service method must be prepared to receive online financial transactions from full service acquirers, and to receive authorization messages followed by deferred clearing transactions from full service and authorization-only acquirers. The full service issuer may choose to manage the cardholder's available balance or credit line by placing a temporary hold on funds until it receives the 0220 advice. Because there could be circumstances in which the issuer does not receive the 0220 advice (for instance, a reversal was not properly processed), the full service issuer may want to establish an expiration date for holds, possibly three to four days after the authorization date. section_new_paragraphs: A purchase transaction is a standard purchase request to authorize, post, and settle a transaction involving the sale of goods or services. Purchase transactions are supported by Visa POS.

Cashback transactions for Visa are included in the flows for this category. A purchase with cashback transaction differs from a purchase by the presence of an amount in Field 61.1— Other Amounts. A purchase with cashback transaction is a variation of the purchase transaction that permits the cardholder to get cash in addition to goods or services. For Visa, purchase with cashback is allowed for domestic transactions only; it is not supported for international transactions. Participating regions may offer a cashback service through VisaNet. Clients can contact their Visa representatives for information about availability. Visa cashback transactions are only allowed in face-to-face POS environments. This transaction is optional for acquirers and for merchants. Merchants that want to support this transaction service establish their own cashback limits. For full service participants outside of the United Kingdom (U.K.), Field 4—Amount, Transaction must contain the total transaction amount, which is the sum of the purchase amount and the cashback amount. For the U.K., a purchase with cashback transaction differs from a purchase by an amount in Field 61.1, positions 1–12—Other Amount, Transaction. Regional Visa Rules can apply to cashback transactions. Keeping the cashback amount separate from the purchase amount allows the issuer to check the desired cashback amount against daily cash withdrawal limits, which may differ from daily purchase limits. If the desired cashback amount causes the daily cash withdrawal limit to be exceeded, or if the combined purchase and cashback amount exceeds the cardholder's available balance but the purchase amount alone does not, the issuer can decline the transaction by using a response code to indicate that the cashback limit was exceeded, and the merchant can send a new transaction for the purchase amount only. A manual cash disbursement is a transaction by which the cardholder obtains cash in a face-to- face environment. It is valid for Visa POS. Purchase requests and manual cash disbursements have financial impact on cardholder accounts. They result in the updating of system settlement totals for the acquirer and issuer. STIP checks cardholder activity using these:
Issuer-specified activity limits (count and amount). Alternative limits designated on the Account Screen Authorization File (ASAF).

The activity check determines whether or not approval of the request causes the card usage to exceed these limits. If the activity is over the specified limits, STIP assigns response code 61 (exceeds approval amount limit). The activity check is based on activity accumulated daily in the Activity File by default, which contains only STIP approvals. Issuers may optionally specify that both issuer and STIP approvals are accumulated in the activity file. VisaNet resets the accumulated totals in the Activity File to zero every 24 hours so that the file always reflects the current day's activity. Activity Checking and Accumulation When a transaction is processed in STIP, V.I.P. performs activity checking and accumulation using the issuer-specified activity limits. Accumulators are running totals of transactions approved in STIP. While issuers specify activity limits at the issuing identifier level, V.I.P. maintains accumulators at the account level. This description of activity checking and accumulation assumes that the combination of issuer specifications and transaction characteristics would result in activity checking being performed, and, that the transaction passed all other STIP tests. A transaction passes activity checking if adding the current transaction to the accumulators would not cause the accumulators to exceed the limits. Failing a limit (activity count, activity, amount, or maximum transaction size) prevents STIP approval. Accumulators are incremented only when the transaction passes all STIP tests, and STIP sends an approval to the acquirer. Transactions approved by the issuer, do not increment accumulators unless the issuer has specified this option. For example: 1.

If the sum of the daily STIP activity count, and preauthorization count plus one (for this transaction) is greater than the STIP limit for the applicable Purchase (POS) or cash category, STIP sets the activity check response to response code 65 (exceeds withdrawal frequency limit). 2. If the sum is not greater than the applicable purchase (POS) or cash activity limit STIP processing continues.

The STIP transaction is approved if it passes all activity checks and other testing, such as authentication services. Non-Standard Activity Checking STIP can perform non-standard activity checking on accounts that the issuer lists in the ASAF as high-risk or as low-risk accounts. If STIP finds a response code listed in the ASAF, it checks the limits in the ASAF instead of the standard activity limits. When STIP Does Not Check Activity
STIP does not perform activity checking in some cases because it is not needed to make an authorization decision. STIP does not perform activity checking in these cases:
The request (for instance, a credit adjustment transaction) results in a credit to the cardholder's account. STIP assigned a decline response code during editing, ASAF checking, or PIN checking.
STIP also does not perform activity checking on these:
Account or address verification requests. Valid preauthorizations.
STIP approves transactions in these instances:

The transaction is a POS preauthorization completion. The transaction is an 0200 original message, not a reversal, and field 3 contains code 20 and field 63.3 is present. The message is an original credit transaction, not declined by Visa, destined for an issuer who supports 0100 original credit transactions and does not support authorization requests.

Excessive Activity STIP responds with response code 65 (exceeds withdrawal frequency limit) if the sum of the STIP activity exceeds the issuer's count limits. STIP responds with response code 61 (exceeds approval amount limit) if:

For a non-preauthorization request, the activity amount is exceeded, but not the activity count. The activity amount is exceeded, but not the activity count. Activity amount and activity count limits are exceeded.

STIP tries to authorize a partial approval for preauthorization service issuing identifiers if the transaction is an 0100 preauthorization and although no counts have been exceeded, the total transaction amount has been exceeded. If the total amount is exceeded, STIP reduces the transaction amount by the cardholder excess amount. The reduced, or partial, amount becomes the amount. However, if the partial amount is greater than the issuer preauthorization limit per transaction, the issuer preauthorization limit amount becomes the amount. changes.old: Reversals cannot be declined. When STIP receives a reversal, it always approves the reversal and creates an advice for the issuer. STIP, however, edits the reversal for validity. STIP checks the reversal for proper syntax and consistency, and searches for the corresponding original transaction being reversed. If STIP finds the original transaction, STIP updates the activity records, and the reversal has financial impact. If STIP does not find the financial record, the reversal has no financial impact so STIP does not update the activity records. The issuer may still receive response code 00 (approved) or the acquirer may receive response code 21 (no action taken). V.I.P. generates a reversal for the issuer if STIP cannot deliver an 0210 response to an approved 0200 request to the acquirer. STIP also generates reversals to the issuer for returned responses or for late responses to approved requests. STIP responds with response code 79 (already reversed) if an acquirer sends a reversal and the history record shows that a previous reversal was processed for the same transaction. This response code value is only used by V.I.P. Issuers must not use this value in response messages. STIP responds with response code 80 (no financial impact) if an acquirer sends a reversal and the history records show that the original request was declined. STIP responds with response code 76 (unsolicited reversal) if there is no history for the transaction in question and the reversal is inter-VIC, or if V.I.P. is in single-center mode.

changes.old: VSS reconciliation reports—VSS reconciliation reports provide totals for all transactions sent to or received from VisaNet, including non-financial transactions such as declines and balance inquiries. The reports provide daily counts for these transactions. VSS settlement reports—VSS settlement reports provide interchange, reimbursement fee, and charge totals settled by VSS. SMS transaction detail reports—Optional SMS transaction detail reports provide an audit trail of all 01xx, 02xx, and 04xx transactions in the day's settlement total. Recipients can use the reports to research differences between totals reported by VisaNet on the VSS reports and those reported by the client's or the processor's system. Point-of-Sale Authorization (POSA) File—The POSA File provides debit and credit transaction data, compiled on a daily basis. Participating acquirers get authorization information that can improve billing accuracy and reduce fraud and dispute losses. The file also provides accurate point-of-entry information, enabling acquirers to differentiate between a transaction originating from a manual key entry from one originating from a proximity payment terminal, and distinguish between a transaction made with a chip card containing a CVV from a transaction made with a chip card without a CVV. Raw data files—Recipients can use raw data files, in conjunction with VSS machine- readable reports, to automate the reconciliation process. As an optional service, Visa provides raw data files that contain detailed information about the settlement day's transactions for a given participant. Raw data is available to all full service issuers and acquirers. Users of this service can use the data to create customized reports and to reconcile data reported by their own systems. Raw data is distinguished from report data in that it is suited for automated processing. The raw data records are produced from the same sources as SMS reports.
